subproblems.title: Level sets of a measure finite on compact sets are null at almost every level (parent step 4, countable_meas_level_set_pos)
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let ν be a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra of Euclid P) with ν(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P, and let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be measurable. Then ν({x : f(x) = t}) = 0 for L¹-almost every t ∈ ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → ℝ), Measurable f → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ν K < ∞) → ∀ᵐ t ∂(volume : Measure ℝ), ν {x | f x = t} = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("ν{f = t} = ν'{f = t} = 0 off a countable set (countable_meas_level_set_pos)"), stated for one measure ν. Write E_t := {x : f(x) = t}.
1. ν is s-finite. By hypothesis ν is finite on every compact set (Mathlib class IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts, built from the hypothesis as ⟨fun K hK => h K hK⟩). ℝ^P is locally compact, so every point has a compact neighbourhood (a closed ball) of finite ν-measure, i.e. ν is locally finite (Mathlib instance isLocallyFiniteMeasure_of_isFiniteMeasureOnCompacts). A locally finite measure on a second-countable space is σ-finite (Mathlib instance sigmaFinite_of_locallyFinite; ℝ^P is second countable), hence s-finite.
2. Countably many charged levels. The sets E_t (t ∈ ℝ) are measurable (f is measurable and singletons of ℝ are measurable) and pairwise disjoint. For an s-finite measure and measurable f, the set S := {t ∈ ℝ : 0 < ν(E_t)} is countable (Mathlib Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos). For completeness: write ν = Σ_n ν_n with finite ν_n; if ν(E_t) > 0 then ν_n(E_t) > 1/m for some n, m ∈ ℕ; for fixed n, m at most m·ν_n(ℝ^P) of the disjoint sets E_t satisfy ν_n(E_t) > 1/m; so S is a countable union of finite sets.
3. A countable subset of ℝ is Lebesgue-null (it is a countable union of null singletons; Set.Countable.measure_zero). Hence L¹(S) = 0.
4. In [0, ∞], ν(E_t) ≠ 0 if and only if 0 < ν(E_t) (pos_iff_ne_zero). Therefore L¹({t : ¬ ν(E_t) = 0}) = L¹(S) = 0, which is exactly the statement that ν(E_t) = 0 for L¹-a.e. t (Mathlib ae_iff). ∎
proof_key_steps: ν is finite on compact sets, hence locally finite and σ-finite (s-finite) on ℝ^P.
Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos: only countably many of the disjoint level sets {f = t} have positive ν-measure.
Countable subsets of ℝ are Lebesgue-null, so ν{f = t} = 0 for a.e. t (ae_iff).

subproblems.statement: Assume (MM), the (MM) part of the conjunct (T1) ∧ (T2) ∧ (MM) of the selected node's dependency foundations (dtc_bc_tc_cl_foundations; verbatim, and also the type of the accepted declaration cbr_slice_mass_majorant): for every P ∈ ℕ, measures μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) on ℝ^P, continuous f : ℝ^P → ℝ, G ⊆ ℝ^P, a, b ∈ ℝ, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and Z_j : ℝ → [0, ∞] with μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}) < ∞ for every j and Z_j(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹) μ_j(G ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all j and all t ∈ (a, b), there is a measurable g : ℝ → [0, ∞] with liminf_{j→∞} Z_j(t) ≤ g(t) for L¹-a.e. t ∈ (a, b) and ∫_{(a,b)} g dL¹ ≤ L · liminf_{j→∞} μ_j(G ∩ {a < f < b}). Let P ∈ ℕ, μ_i (i ∈ ℕ) measures on ℝ^P, f : ℝ^P → ℝ continuous, L ∈ ℝ≥0 and Z_{i,k}(t) ∈ [0, ∞] (i, k ∈ ℕ, t ∈ ℝ); write W_k := B_{k+1}(0) (open ball of radius k + 1 about 0). Suppose sup_i μ_i(W_k) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ, and Z_{i,k}(t) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹) μ_i(W_k ∩ {t − h < f < t}) for all i, k ∈ ℕ and all t ∈ ℝ (liminf along 𝓝[>]0, values in [0, ∞]). Then for L¹-a.e. t ∈ ℝ, liminf_{i→∞} Z_{i,k}(t) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ.

subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof ("(MM) with μ_i + μ'_i, G := W_k, (a, b) := (−m, m) gives, for a.e. t, liminf_i(M_{W_k}(Z_{i,t}) + M_{W_k}(∂B_{i,t})) < ∞ for all k"), written for arbitrary measures μ_i and majorized functions Z_{i,k}. Put Λ_k := sup_i μ_i(W_k) < ∞.
1. Fix k, m ∈ ℕ and E := W_k ∩ {−m < f < m}. For every j, μ_j(E) ≤ μ_j(W_k) ≤ Λ_k < ∞ (measure_mono with E ⊆ W_k, and le_iSup). Apply (MM) with P, the measures μ_j, the continuous f, G := W_k, (a, b) := (−m, m), L and Z_j := Z_{j,k} (as functions of t). Its finiteness hypothesis is the bound just proved, and its majorant hypothesis is the assumed inequality for Z_{j,k}(t), used only for t ∈ (−m, m). (MM) yields a measurable g = g_{k,m} : ℝ → [0, ∞] with (α) for L¹-a.e. t: t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) ≤ g(t); and (β) ∫_{(−m,m)} g dL¹ ≤ L · liminf_j μ_j(E).
2. The right side of (β) is finite: every term μ_j(E) is ≤ Λ_k, so liminf_j μ_j(E) ≤ Λ_k (Filter.liminf_le_of_frequently_le'), Λ_k < ∞ and L < ∞, hence L · liminf_j μ_j(E) ≠ ∞ (ENNReal.mul_ne_top). So ∫ g d(L¹ restricted to (−m, m)) ≠ ∞, and since g is measurable, g(t) < ∞ for (L¹ restricted to (−m, m))-a.e. t (Mathlib ae_lt_top). As (−m, m) is measurable (measurableSet_Ioo), this means (ae_restrict_iff'): for L¹-a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies g(t) < ∞.
3. Intersecting the two full-measure sets of (α) and step 2: for L¹-a.e. t, t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) ≤ g(t) < ∞.
4. Still for fixed k: a countable intersection of full-measure sets has full measure (ae_all_iff over m ∈ ℕ), so for L¹-a.e. t, for every m ∈ ℕ, t ∈ (−m, m) implies liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞. For such t choose m ∈ ℕ with m > |t| (exists_nat_gt); then −m < t < m (neg_abs_le, le_abs_self), so liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞. Thus for each k, liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞ for L¹-a.e. t.
5. Applying ae_all_iff once more, over k ∈ ℕ, gives: for L¹-a.e. t, liminf_j Z_{j,k}(t) < ∞ for every k ∈ ℕ. ∎
proof_key_steps: For each k, m apply (MM) with G := B_{k+1}(0) and (a, b) := (−m, m); finiteness from sup_i μ_i(B_{k+1}(0)) < ∞.
∫_{(−m,m)} g ≤ L · sup_i μ_i(W_k) < ∞, so the measurable majorant g is a.e. finite on (−m, m) (ae_lt_top, ae_restrict_iff').
Countable intersection over m (the intervals (−m, m) exhaust ℝ) and then over k (ae_all_iff).

2. boundaryMassOn(Z_t, W) = boundaryMassOn(B_t, W). If m = 0 both sides are 0 by the definition of boundaryMassOn. If m = e + 1, let ζ ∈ 𝒟^e(U). (b) boundaryMassOn(S|_V, W) ≤ boundaryMassOn(S, W'): if m = 0 both sides are 0; if m = e + 1, (S|_V).boundary = (S.boundary)|_V, because both send η ∈ 𝒟^e(V) to S evaluated at a test form whose underlying form is dη (GeometricCurrentOn.ext; the two values agree definitionally), so the claim is (a) applied to S.boundary.
2. Z has locally finite mass. Let W be open with closure(W) compact. A compact set is bounded, so closure(W) ⊆ B_r(0) for some r (IsCompact.isBounded, Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball); choose k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ r (exists_nat_ge); then W ⊆ closure(W) ⊆ B_r(0) ⊆ W_k. By monotonicity of mass in the region (GeometricCurrentOn.massOn_mono), lower semicontinuity of mass under weak convergence (SimonGMT WeaklyConvergesOn.massOn_le_liminf) and M ≤ M + boundaryMassOn (liminf_le_liminf with le_self_add): M_W(Z) ≤ M_{W_k}(Z) ≤ liminf_i M_{W_k}(Z_i) ≤ liminf_i u_{i,k} < ∞.
3. Z|_{B_1(x)} is IM for every x ∈ ℝ^P. Choose k ∈ ℕ with k ≥ |x|; then B_1(x) ⊆ W_k, since |y − x| < 1 gives |y| ≤ |y − x| + |x| < 1 + k (ball_subset_ball' with dist(x, 0) = |x|). Since liminf_i u_{i,k} < ∞, choose C with liminf_i u_{i,k} < C < ∞ (exists_between). Then u_{i,k} < C for frequently many i in atTop (Filter.frequently_lt_of_liminf_lt; its coboundedness side condition holds automatically in [0, ∞]), so there is a strictly increasing ψ : ℕ → ℕ with u_{ψ(l),k} ≤ C for all l (Filter.extraction_of_frequently_atTop). Put Y_l := Z_{ψ(l)}|_{B_1(x)} and Y := Z|_{B_1(x)} in 𝒟_d(B_1(x)).
(i) Every Y_l is IM, by IML_P(d)(2) with U := ℝ^P (open), V := B_1(x) (open) and X := Z_{ψ(l)}.
(ii) Y_l ⇀ Y in B_1(x): for ω ∈ 𝒟^d(B_1(x)), Y_l(ω) = Z_{ψ(l)}(ω~) → Z(ω~) = Y(ω), since (Z_{ψ(l)}(ω~))_l is a subsequence of the convergent sequence (Z_i(ω~))_i (ψ is strictly increasing, so ψ(l) → ∞).
(iii) Let W'' be open with closure(W'') compact and contained in B_1(x). Then W'' ⊆ closure(W'') ⊆ B_1(x) ⊆ W_k, so by 1(a) and 1(b), for every l, M_{W''}(Y_l) + boundaryMassOn(Y_l, W'') ≤ M_{W_k}(Z_{ψ(l)}) + boundaryMassOn(Z_{ψ(l)}, W_k) = u_{ψ(l),k} ≤ C. Hence sup_l (M_{W''}(Y_l) + boundaryMassOn(Y_l, W'')) ≤ C < ∞ (iSup_le).
By CL_P(d) applied with U := B_1(x) (open), T_l := Y_l and T := Y, the current Z|_{B_1(x)} is IM.
4. Conclusion. By step 2 and step 3 (with r := 1 > 0 and B_1(x) ⊆ ℝ^P at every x ∈ ℝ^P), IML_P(d)(1) applied with U := ℝ^P (open) and X := Z shows that Z is IM. ∎
proof_key_steps: Domain restriction does not increase M_W or boundaryMassOn, and the boundary commutes with restriction (degree case split on a fresh m).
Lower semicontinuity: M_W(Z) ≤ liminf_i (M_{W_k}(Z_i) + boundaryMassOn(Z_i, W_k)) < ∞ for W ⊆ W_k, so Z has locally finite mass.

For x ∈ ℝ^P take k ≥ |x| and a subsequence ψ with M_{W_k}(Z_{ψ(l)}) + boundaryMassOn(Z_{ψ(l)}, W_k) ≤ C; the IM restrictions Z_{ψ(l)}|_{B_1(x)} converge weakly to Z|_{B_1(x)} with bounded mass and boundary mass, so CL_P(d) on B_1(x) gives Z|_{B_1(x)} IM.
IML_P(d)(1) glues the local statements: Z is IM.

subproblems.title: Boundary-mass bound for the slice of a represented boundary (reuse of accepted dmcbr_sl_sb_boundaryMassOn_slice_le)
subproblems.statement: Assume (SL), whose Lean type is byte-identical to that of the selected node's accepted dependency slicing (cmc_slice_mass_bounds) and of dimred_mbl_slice_mass_bounds (first hypothesis of the Lean statement; content as in sibling slice_sum_bound). Let P, m ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P open, T ∈ 𝒟_{m+1}(U), μ a measure on ℝ^P with μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, and ξ : ℝ^P → Λ_m(ℝ^P) a.e. strongly measurable for μ with |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| for every m-covector α, for μ-a.e. x. Assume ∂T(η) = ∫ξ(x)(η(x))dμ(x) for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U). Let f : ℝ^P → ℝ be L-Lipschitz (L ∈ ℝ≥0), t ∈ ℝ, W ⊆ ℝ^P open, and B ∈ 𝒟_m(U) with B(η) = ∫_{f<t}ξ(x)(η(x))dμ(x) for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U). Then boundaryMassOn(B, W) ≤ L · liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) (liminf along 𝓝[>]0, in [0, ∞]; boundaryMassOn(B, W) = 0 if m = 0 and = M_W(∂B) if m ≥ 1).
subproblems.lean_statement: (∀ (P k : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (μ μ' : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P (k + 1)) (ξ' : Euclid P → MultiVector P k) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal), IsOpen U → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ' K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ' μ' → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) (k + 1), |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ', ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) k, |ξ' x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn U (k + 1), T ω = ∫ x, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k + 1)) x) ∂μ) → (∀ η : TestFormOn U k, T.boundary η = ∫ x, ξ' x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ') → LipschitzWith L f → ∃ (A : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn U (k + 1)) (B : ℝ → GeometricCurrentOn U k), (∀ (t : ℝ) (ω : TestFormOn U (k + 1)), A t ω = ∫ x in {x | f x < t}, ξ x ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (k + 1)) x) ∂μ) ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (η : TestFormOn U k), B t η = ∫ x in {x | f x < t}, ξ' x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k) x) ∂μ') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (η : TestFormOn U k), Disjoint (tsupport (η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) k)) {x | f x = t} → (A t).boundary η = B t η) ∧ (∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (t : ℝ), IsOpen W → ((A t).boundary - B t).massOn W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ (W ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)) ∧ (∀ (W : Set (Euclid P)) (a b : ℝ), IsOpen W → ∫⁻ t in Ioo a b, ((A t).boundary - B t).massOn W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * μ (W ∩ {x | a < f x ∧ f x < b}))) → ∀ (P m : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U (m + 1)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ξ : Euclid P → MultiVector P m) (f : Euclid P → ℝ) (L : NNReal) (t : ℝ) (B : GeometricCurrentOn U m) (W : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → IsOpen W → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → μ K < ∞) → AEStronglyMeasurable ξ μ → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) m, |ξ x α| ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α) → (∀ η : TestFormOn U m, T.boundary η = ∫ x, ξ x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μ) → LipschitzWith L f → (∀ η : TestFormOn U m, B η = ∫ x in {x | f x < t}, ξ x ((η : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) m) x) ∂μ) → boundaryMassOn B W ≤ (L : ℝ≥0∞) * liminf (fun h : ℝ => ENNReal.ofReal h⁻¹ * μ (W ∩ {x | t - h < f x ∧ f x < t})) (𝓝[>] 0)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Write S_h := W ∩ {t − h < f < t} and ℓ := liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(S_h), the liminf taken along 𝓝[>]0 in [0, ∞]. The claim is boundaryMassOn(B, W) ≤ L·ℓ.
1. Case m = 0. For a 0-dimensional current, boundaryMassOn(B, W) = 0 by definition, and 0 ≤ L·ℓ in [0, ∞].
2. Case m = m' + 1. By definition boundaryMassOn(B, W) = M_W(∂B), where ∂B ∈ 𝒟_{m'}(U). Put Y := ∂T ∈ 𝒟_{m'+1}(U).
3. Representations. By hypothesis, Y(ω) = ∂T(ω) = ∫ ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m'+1}(U). Moreover ∂Y = ∂∂T = 0 (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_boundary). Write 0 for both the zero measure on ℝ^P and the zero field ℝ^P → Λ_{m'}(ℝ^P). Then for every ζ ∈ 𝒟^{m'}(U), ∂Y(ζ) = 0 = ∫ 0(x)(ζ(x)) d0(x), because an integral with respect to the zero measure vanishes (Mathlib integral_zero_measure).
4. Hypotheses of (SL). Apply (SL) with k := m', the open set U, T := Y, (μ, ξ), (μ', ξ') := (0, 0), f and L. Its hypotheses hold:
- U is open.
- μ(K) < ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U, by hypothesis.
- The zero measure gives every set measure 0 < ∞.
- ξ is a.e. strongly measurable for μ, by hypothesis.
- Every function is a.e. strongly measurable for the zero measure (Mathlib aestronglyMeasurable_zero_measure), in particular the zero field.
- The bound |ξ(x)(α)| ≤ |α| holds for μ-a.e. x, by hypothesis.
- The bound for the zero field holds 0-a.e., because the almost-everywhere filter of the zero measure is ⊥ (Mathlib ae_zero), so every property holds 0-a.e.
- The two representation identities are those of step 3.
- f is L-Lipschitz.
5. Conclusions of (SL). There are families A'_s ∈ 𝒟_{m'+1}(U) and B'_s ∈ 𝒟_{m'}(U) (s ∈ ℝ) with:
(i) A'_s(ω) = ∫_{f<s} ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) for all s and all ω ∈ 𝒟^{m'+1}(U);
(ii) B'_s(ζ) = ∫_{f<s} 0(x)(ζ(x)) d0(x) for all s and all ζ ∈ 𝒟^{m'}(U);
(iii) M_{W'}(∂A'_s − B'_s) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W' ∩ {s − h < f < s}) for every open W' and every s.
The two remaining conclusions of (SL) are not needed.
6. Identification at s = t. By (i) and the hypothesis on B, A'_t(ω) = ∫_{f<t} ξ(x)(ω(x)) dμ(x) = B(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^{m'+1}(U). Currents are determined by their values (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.ext), so A'_t = B. By (ii), B'_t(ζ) is an integral with respect to the restriction of the zero measure, which is the zero measure, so B'_t(ζ) = 0 = 0(ζ) for every ζ, and B'_t = 0 by ext. Finally, subtraction of currents is pointwise, so (∂B − 0)(ζ) = ∂B(ζ) − 0 = ∂B(ζ) for every ζ. Hence ∂A'_t − B'_t = ∂B − 0 = ∂B by ext.
7. Apply (iii) with W' := W, which is open by hypothesis, and s := t. This gives boundaryMassOn(B, W) = M_W(∂B) = M_W(∂A'_t − B'_t) ≤ L·liminf_{h→0+} ofReal(h⁻¹)·μ(W ∩ {t − h < f < t}) = L·ℓ. ∎
proof_key_steps: If m = 0, then boundaryMassOn(B, W) = 0 by definition.
If m = m' + 1, then (μ, ξ) represents ∂T and the zero measure with the zero field represents ∂∂T = 0. These satisfy all finiteness, measurability and a.e.-bound hypotheses of (SL).
(SL) applied to ∂T gives A', B' with A'_t = B and B'_t = 0 (GeometricCurrentOn.ext) and M_W(∂A'_t − B'_t) ≤ L·liminf h⁻¹μ(W ∩ {t−h<f<t}).
∂A'_t − B'_t = ∂B, so boundaryMassOn(B, W) = M_W(∂B) satisfies the bound.

subproblems.title: Local mass is invariant under negation of a current (reuse of accepted dmcbr_sl_sb_massOn_eq_of_apply_eq_neg)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set, T₁, T₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn U n) and W ⊆ ℝ^P an arbitrary set. If T₁(ω) = −T₂(ω) for every test form ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (TestFormOn U n), then M_W(T₁) = M_W(T₂). Here M_W(T) = T.massOn W ∈ [0, ∞] is the supremum of ENNReal.ofReal(T(ω)) over the admissible forms ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), i.e. those with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ ℝ^P (massAdmissibleOn U n W, |·| the Euclidean covector norm covectorEuclideanNorm).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (T₁ T₂ : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (W : Set (Euclid P)), (∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, T₁ ω = -T₂ ω) → T₁.massOn W = T₂.massOn W
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation. For S ∈ 𝒟_n(U), M_W(S) = S.massOn W = sup{ofReal(S(ω)) : ω ∈ 𝒜} in [0, ∞]. Here 𝒜 := massAdmissibleOn U n W is the set of ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ 1 for every x ∈ ℝ^P, where |·| = covectorEuclideanNorm.
1. 𝒜 is closed under negation. Let ω ∈ 𝒜. Since 𝒟^n(U) is a submodule of the n-forms, −ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), and the underlying form of −ω is x ↦ −ω(x). Hence tsupport(−ω) = tsupport(ω) ⊆ W (Mathlib tsupport_neg). For every x, |(−ω)(x)| = |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| ≤ 1 (SimonGMT covectorEuclideanNorm_neg). So −ω ∈ 𝒜.
2. Auxiliary inequality. Let S₁, S₂ ∈ 𝒟_n(U) satisfy S₁(ω) = −S₂(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U), and let ω ∈ 𝒜. The functional underlying S₂ is ℝ-linear, so S₂(−ω) = −S₂(ω) = S₁(ω). By step 1, −ω ∈ 𝒜, so ofReal(S₁(ω)) = ofReal(S₂(−ω)) ≤ M_W(S₂), because every admissible value is at most the supremum (SimonGMT GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn). Since ω ∈ 𝒜 was arbitrary, M_W(S₂) bounds every value whose supremum is M_W(S₁). Hence M_W(S₁) ≤ M_W(S₂).
3. By hypothesis T₁(ω) = −T₂(ω) for every ω, so step 2 applies with (S₁, S₂) := (T₁, T₂) and gives M_W(T₁) ≤ M_W(T₂).
4. For every ω, T₂(ω) = −(−T₂(ω)) = −T₁(ω). So step 2 also applies with (S₁, S₂) := (T₂, T₁) and gives M_W(T₂) ≤ M_W(T₁).
5. By antisymmetry of ≤ on [0, ∞], M_W(T₁) = M_W(T₂). ∎
proof_key_steps: Admissible forms for M_W are closed under negation: tsupport(−ω) = tsupport ω (tsupport_neg) and |−ω(x)| = |ω(x)| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
If S₁ = −S₂ pointwise, then by linearity ofReal(S₁(ω)) = ofReal(S₂(−ω)) ≤ M_W(S₂) for each admissible ω, so M_W(S₁) ≤ M_W(S₂).
Apply this to (T₁, T₂) and to (T₂, T₁), using T₂ = −T₁ pointwise, and conclude by antisymmetry.

subproblems.title: Superadditivity of liminf in [0, ∞] (reuse of accepted dmcbr_sl_sb_ennreal_liminf_add_le)
subproblems.statement: For every type ι (in Lean's universe Type), every filter F on ι and all functions u, v : ι → [0, ∞] (ℝ≥0∞), liminf_F u + liminf_F v ≤ liminf_F (i ↦ u(i) + v(i)), where liminf is Mathlib's Filter.liminf in the complete lattice ℝ≥0∞.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (ι : Type) (F : Filter ι) (u v : ι → ℝ≥0∞), liminf u F + liminf v F ≤ liminf (fun i => u i + v i) F
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. [0, ∞] is a complete lattice, so for every w : ι → [0, ∞], liminf_F w = sup_{s ∈ F} inf_{i ∈ s} w(i) (Mathlib Filter.liminf_eq_iSup_iInf). Apply this to u, v and w := (i ↦ u(i) + v(i)). Write a(s) := inf_{i∈s} u(i), b(s) := inf_{i∈s} v(i) and Λ := liminf_F w = sup_{r∈F} inf_{i∈r} (u(i) + v(i)). The claim becomes sup_{s∈F} a(s) + sup_{s'∈F} b(s') ≤ Λ.
2. Pairwise bound. Let s, s' ∈ F. For each i ∈ s ∩ s', a(s) ≤ u(i) because i ∈ s, and b(s') ≤ v(i) because i ∈ s'. Since addition is monotone in [0, ∞], a(s) + b(s') ≤ u(i) + v(i). Taking the infimum over i ∈ s ∩ s' gives a(s) + b(s') ≤ inf_{i ∈ s∩s'} (u(i) + v(i)). As F is a filter, s ∩ s' ∈ F, so this infimum is one of the terms of the supremum Λ. Therefore a(s) + b(s') ≤ Λ.
3. Both index families are nonempty because univ ∈ F. In [0, ∞], adding a constant commutes with nonempty suprema. This gives the following: if p and q are predicates, some i satisfies p, some j satisfies q, and f(i) + g(j) ≤ c whenever p(i) and q(j), then (sup_{p(i)} f(i)) + (sup_{q(j)} g(j)) ≤ c (Mathlib ENNReal.biSup_add_biSup_le'). Apply it with p = q = (· ∈ F), f = a, g = b and c = Λ; its main hypothesis is step 2. This gives sup_{s∈F} a(s) + sup_{s'∈F} b(s') ≤ Λ.
4. By step 1, this inequality is liminf_F u + liminf_F v ≤ liminf_F (i ↦ u(i) + v(i)). No finiteness or boundedness assumption is used, and the argument also covers the trivial filter. ∎
proof_key_steps: liminf_F w = sup_{s∈F} inf_{i∈s} w(i) in the complete lattice [0, ∞] (liminf_eq_iSup_iInf).
For s, s' ∈ F: inf_s u + inf_{s'} v ≤ inf_{s∩s'} (u + v) ≤ liminf_F (u + v), since s ∩ s' ∈ F.
The index families are nonempty (univ ∈ F), so ENNReal.biSup_add_biSup_le' turns the pairwise bound into liminf_F u + liminf_F v ≤ liminf_F (u + v).
